entities.name: Adalgar
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Adalgar (died 909) was Archbishop of Hamburg-Bremen from 888 to 909, leading one of the most important missionary sees in Northern Europe during one of its most difficult periods — the era of Viking raids that devastated many of the regions Hamburg-Bremen was responsible for Christianising. His archiepiscopate came directly after the death of Rimbert, the biographer of Saint Ansgar and a significant missionary bishop in his own right.

Adalgar's tenure coincided with the worst period of Viking disruption to the Carolingian-era missionary work in Scandinavia. The raids that had been attacking Frankish territory since the 840s had also severely disrupted the fragile Christian communities that had been established in Denmark and Sweden through Ansgar's and Rimbert's missions. The question of how to maintain and advance Christian mission under Viking pressure defined Adalgar's archiepiscopate.

His archiepiscopate also coincided with the political fragmentation of the Carolingian Empire following its division among Louis the Pious's sons and the further weakening of central authority under later Carolingians. The church that Hamburg-Bremen had built under Carolingian imperial patronage had to adapt to a world of rival kings and weakened imperial support. Adalgar's navigation of these challenges maintained the see's institutional continuity until the more stable conditions of the Ottonian era.
